Apply conditioner and let it sit: Work the hydrating conditioner into their coat in the same direction of hair growth, focusing on the ends of the hair which are most prone to dryness and breakage. 8. Rinse conditioner and pat dry: Rinse all conditioner from the coat until water runs clear, then lift your dog out of the tub and place them on a microfiber towel. Pat (don't rub) their coat to absorb excess water, squeezing gently to remove moisture without tangling the hair. Do not use regular cotton towels, as they can cause friction that leads to frizz and mats. This step takes ~3-4 minutes.
9. Blow dry the coat completely to prevent mats: Set your force dryer to the low heat, high airflow setting, holding it 6-8 inches away from their skin to avoid burns. 1. Gather all required products and tools first to avoid leaving your dog unattended mid-process. Recommended products: hypoallergenic Maltese-specific whitening shampoo (e.g., Isle of Dogs Everyday Silky Coating Shampoo, avoid human shampoos which disrupt skin pH), hydrating conditioner (e.g., Chris Christensen Ice on Ice Conditioner), leave-in detangler spray, pet-safe ear cleaning solution, tear stain eye wipes. Tools: soft-pin slicker brush for sensitive skin, dual-sided stainless steel greyhound comb (wide and narrow tooth), rubber non-slip bath mat, super absorbent microfiber towels, low-heat high-airflow force blow dryer, cotton balls for ear protection, non-slip grooming table (optional but recommended). This step takes ~5 minutes.
2. Prep your dog before bathing: Brush through their entire coat thoroughly with the slicker brush, then follow with the greyhound comb to remove any pre-existing tangles or mats. For stubborn knots, spritz detangler spray and gently work them apart with your fingers rather than pulling to avoid hurting your dog. Place cotton balls in their ears to block water from entering the ear canal, and wipe around their eyes with pet-safe eye wipes to remove existing tear stains before getting them wet. This step takes ~10-15 minutes depending on coat length and matting level.
3. Prepare the bath area: Fill a tub or sink with 2-3 inches of lukewarm water (test the temperature with your wrist to ensure it is around 100°F/38°C, not too hot for your Maltese's sensitive skin). Place a rubber non-slip mat on the bottom of the tub to keep your dog comfortable and prevent slipping while bathing. This step takes ~2 minutes.
4. Wet your dog's coat thoroughly: Use a handheld shower head or plastic cup to pour water over their body, starting from their neck and moving down to their tail, avoiding their face and ears initially. Ensure the coat is saturated all the way to the skin, as Maltese hair is dense and can repel water if not fully soaked through. This step takes ~2-3 minutes.
5. Apply shampoo and lather gently: Dilute your chosen Maltese-specific shampoo with equal parts warm water to prevent over-concentration that can irritate their skin. Massage the lather into their coat in the direction of hair growth, working from the neck down to the paws, being careful not to rub in circular motions that can cause tangles. Avoid getting shampoo in their eyes, ears, or mouth. This step takes ~3-5 minutes.
6. Rinse the shampoo completely: Use lukewarm water to rinse all suds from their coat, again working from top to bottom, until the water runs completely clear. Any leftover shampoo residue can cause skin irritation, dryness, or matting later, so take extra care to rinse the belly, armpits, and groin areas where shampoo often gets trapped. This step takes ~4-6 minutes.
7. Apply conditioner and let it penetrate: Work the hydrating conditioner into their coat in the same direction of hair growth, focusing on the ends of the hair which are most prone to dryness and breakage. Let the conditioner sit for 3-5 minutes as directed on the product label to allow it to penetrate the hair cuticle and add moisture that prevents tangles during drying. This step takes ~3-5 minutes including wait time.
8. Rinse conditioner and pat excess water dry: Rinse all conditioner from the coat until the water runs completely clear, then lift your dog out of the tub and place them on a large microfiber towel. Pat (do not rub) their coat to absorb excess water, squeezing gently to remove moisture without tangling the hair. Avoid regular cotton towels, as they cause friction that leads to frizz and mats. This step takes ~3-4 minutes.
9. Blow dry the coat fully to prevent mat formation: Set your force dryer to the low heat, high airflow setting, holding it 6-8 inches away from their skin to avoid burns. Work in 2-3 inch small sections, brushing the hair with the slicker brush as you dry, pulling the hair straight gently in the direction of growth. Keep drying until the coat is 100% dry, as any leftover dampness will lead to mats and mildew near the skin. This step takes ~15-25 minutes depending on coat length.
10. Final detangle and finishing touches: Once fully dry, run the dual-sided greyhound comb through the entire coat to catch any remaining tangles, then spritz a small amount of leave-in detangler spray to keep the coat soft and prevent mats from forming between grooming sessions. Remove the cotton balls from their ears, do a final wipe around their eyes, and reward your dog with a treat for good behavior. This step takes ~3-5 minutes.

The entire bathing and drying process typically takes 50-75 minutes total depending on coat length and how much pre-existing matting is present, and sticking to this routine every 2-3 weeks will keep your Maltese's coat silky, healthy, and tangle-free long-term.
